requiredFindings.title: Correct J4a's predicted census delta to four point names
requiredFindings.problem: RW.3 predicts that J4a's RW-K4 and RW-K7 states add 8 census points and 8 kill-set points. The two preceding bullets name only four distinct durability points: before/after directory-barrier in each of two repair scopes, each with two occurrences. The matrix census counts distinct names, so this is four census points, eight trace events and eight sampled kill-set points. RW.7 requires J4e to match RW.3 and stop on a contradiction, so the stated eight-point census delta would reject the correctly transcribed census.

evidence.detail: K4 adds directory-barrier.before and .after under x3c.ledger-create.projects.repair, each with two occurrences.
K7 has the same two-name shape under x3b.floor.directory.repair.
Census::from_exit increments occurrences on the existing same-name point and adds a new CensusPoint only for a new name.
census_json emits one points array entry per CensusPoint, with its separate occurrences member.
censusPoints is len(census.points); kill_set at lines 173-180 samples occurrence ordinals separately.
J4e must match the RW.3 prediction; line 2532 makes any contradiction a stop requiring a further law correction.

requiredFindings.requestedChange: State that J4a's two repair start states contribute four new census point names, each occurring twice, hence eight physical durability events and eight kill-set points. Keep the eight RW-K rows unchanged. Use the four-name census delta in every related prediction/gate; other units' contributions remain to be derived from their own censuses.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: The checker does not require every dynamic census scope as a releaseAbsence.strings entry. At 43ea32a, registry() returns only static SCOPES; check_set uses wanted={OPENSIP_X9_, *scopes}, and the release scan uses those same registered parent strings. Adding repair census points does not extend that list.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Correct the explanation to say the existing scan covers registered owner prefixes, which occur in every full repair scope name, together with the feature-disabled macro's bare-block expansion. If explicit dynamic-name scan entries are intended instead, assign that extension to J4e.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNonBlocking: The existing registered-prefix byte scan covers the full names' prefixes; the source guard also removes repair instrumentation in a release build. This is an inaccurate explanation of existing coverage, not an identified release leak.

nonBlockingObservations.observation: LD-RW-11 deliberately defers narrowing L11's reason until J4e, whereas accepted J-RW r4 item 10 at line 651 says the interim reason names states not yet covered by a passing row. The conservative intermediate reason and passing RW-F00 records are a reasonable staging choice; the retirement gate itself is unchanged.
nonBlockingObservations.recommendation: Include this explicit recording-policy refinement in the owed J-RW record revision alongside LD-RW-6, so the interim L11 wording is not described as a verbatim transcription of r4's reason-update sentence.
